unit: Unit 2: AS 29 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction and Purpose of AS 29
explain: AS 29 (Revised) came into effect for accounting periods starting on or after April 1, 2004.
The primary objective is to lay down recognition criteria and measurement bases for provisions and contingent liabilities.
It prevents 'profit smoothing', where entities arbitrarily create or reverse provisions to manipulate profits between years.
It also establishes appropriate accounting principles for contingent assets.

flow.title: How Profit Smoothing is Prevented
steps: Management reverses provision to boost profit
AS 29 rules stop arbitrary provision creation

topics.example: A company earns heavy profits in 20X1 and wants to create an unnecessary warranty provision to show lower profit and reduce tax; AS 29 prohibits this.
remember: Effective date of AS 29 (Revised) is 1-4-2004.
Profit smoothing means manipulating reported profits by arbitrary creation and reversal of provisions.
mistakes: Assuming management can create provisions freely in high-profit years to build secret reserves.

quiz.q: When did AS 29 (Revised) come into effect?
quiz.why: AS 29 (Revised) became effective for accounting periods commencing on or after 1-4-2004.

quiz.q: What practice does AS 29 specifically aim to eliminate?
quiz.why: AS 29 eliminates profit smoothing where companies create arbitrary provisions to hide true profit fluctuations.

topics.title: Scope of AS 29
explain: AS 29 applies to accounting for provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets with specific exclusions.
Exclusion 1: Financial instruments carried at fair value.
Exclusion 2: Executory contracts, except where the contract is onerous.
Exclusion 3: Insurance contracts in insurance enterprises with policyholders.
Exclusion 4: Items covered by specific standards like AS 7 (Construction), AS 9 (Revenue), AS 15 (Employee Benefits), AS 19 (Leases), or AS 22 (Taxes).

flow.title: Scope Applicability Test
steps: Check if covered by specific standard (AS 7, 9, 15, 19, 22)
Check if financial instrument at fair value
If no exclusions apply use AS 29

topics.example: Employee gratuity liabilities are governed by AS 15 (Employee Benefits), so AS 29 rules do not apply to them.
remember: Executory contracts fall under AS 29 ONLY if they become onerous.
Specific standards like AS 15 or AS 19 override AS 29.
mistakes: Applying AS 29 to employee benefit provisions instead of AS 15.

quiz.q: When does an executory contract fall under the scope of AS 29?
quiz.why: Executory contracts are excluded from AS 29 except when the contract becomes onerous.

quiz.q: Which standard governs employee benefit provisions instead of AS 29?
quiz.why: Provisions for employee benefits are specifically covered by AS 15, excluding them from AS 29.

topics.title: Key Definitions under AS 29
explain: Executory contracts: Contracts where neither party has performed obligations or both have partially performed equally.
Provision: A liability which can be measured only by using a substantial degree of estimation.
Liability: A present obligation arising from past events, settlement of which expects an economic outflow.
Obligating event: An event creating an obligation that leaves the enterprise no realistic alternative to settling.
Present obligation: Obligation whose existence at the balance sheet date is considered probable (>50% chance).
Possible obligation: Obligation whose existence at the balance sheet date is considered not probable.

flow.title: From Past Event to Provision Definition

topics.example: A firm sells goods with a 6-month repair warranty; the past sale is the obligating event requiring a provision estimated from historical repair data.
remember: Provision = Liability requiring substantial estimation.
Present obligation = Probable (>50% chance of existing at balance sheet date).
mistakes: Confusing a possible obligation (not probable) with a present obligation (probable).

quiz.q: How is a Provision defined under AS 29?
o: A reserve for future unknown expansion
A liability measured using substantial estimation
A possible asset from legal cases
A contingent claim disclosed in notes
quiz.why: A provision is defined as a liability which can be measured only by using a substantial degree of estimation.

quiz.q: What is an obligating event?
o: An event where the entity can easily avoid payment
An event creating no realistic alternative to settling
An event happening after balance sheet approval
quiz.why: An obligating event leaves the enterprise with no realistic alternative to settling the obligation.

topics.title: Recognition Criteria for Provisions
explain: A provision must be recognized ONLY when ALL three criteria are satisfied simultaneously:
Condition 1: An enterprise has a present obligation as a result of a past event.
Condition 2: It is probable (>50% chance) that an outflow of economic resources will be required to settle it.
Condition 3: A reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation.
If any condition is missing, NO provision should be recognized.

flow.title: 3-Condition Recognition Checklist
steps: If any NO do not recognize

topics.example: X Ltd sells refrigerators with a 6-month free repair warranty. Since defects occur and repair costs can be estimated, X Ltd must recognize a provision.
remember: All 3 criteria (Present obligation, Probable outflow, Reliable estimate) must be met together.
mistakes: Recognizing a provision when an outflow is merely possible (<50%) rather than probable (>50%).

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a condition required to recognize a provision?
o: Present obligation from a past event
quiz.why: Virtual certainty of inflow relates to contingent assets, not provision recognition criteria.

quiz.q: What should be done if a present obligation exists but economic outflow is NOT probable?
o: Disclose a contingent liability unless remote
Do nothing and make no disclosure
quiz.why: If economic outflow is not probable, a contingent liability is disclosed unless the outflow possibility is remote.

topics.title: Past Event and Probable Outflow Criteria
explain: A past event becomes an obligating event only if the enterprise has no realistic alternative to settling the obligation.
Provisions are recognized only for existing obligations arising from past events, NOT for future operating costs.
Obligations existing independently of future business conduct include penalties or environmental cleanup costs.
A proposed law becomes an obligating event only when the legislation is virtually certain to be enacted.
Outflow is regarded as probable if the probability that the event will occur is greater than the probability that it will not (>50%).
For product warranties, probability of outflow is determined by evaluating the class of obligations as a whole.

flow.title: Evaluating a Past Obligating Event
steps: Can entity avoid cost by future actions?
If YES no present obligation exists
Check if law enactment is virtually certain

topics.example: An oil company pollutes land; if a clean-up law is virtually certain to be passed shortly after year-end, a provision for clean-up must be recognized.
remember: Probable means > 50% probability of occurrence.
Future operational expenses cannot be provided for today.
mistakes: Creating a provision for fitting factory smoke filters required in future, as the entity can avoid it by changing operations.

quiz.q: When does a proposed new law create a present obligation under AS 29?
o: When it is introduced in parliament
When it is virtually certain to be enacted
quiz.why: An obligation arises under a proposed law only when the legislation is virtually certain to be enacted.

quiz.q: What is the threshold for an outflow to be considered 'probable' under AS 29?
quiz.why: Outflow is probable if the event's occurrence is more likely than its non-occurrence (>50%).

topics.title: Reliable Estimate & Contingent Liabilities
explain: Estimates are normal in financial statements; cases where no reliable estimate can be made are extremely rare.
If in an extremely rare case no reliable estimate can be made, the liability is disclosed as a contingent liability.
A Contingent Liability is a possible obligation OR a present obligation not recognized because outflow is not probable or estimate is unreliable.
Contingent liabilities are NOT recognized in the Balance Sheet; they are disclosed in notes unless outflow is remote.
For joint and several liabilities, the portion expected to be met by other parties is disclosed as a contingent liability.

flow.title: Contingent Liability Decision Logic
steps: If NO to any except remote disclose contingent liability

topics.example: AB Ltd receives a legal claim of ₹5,00,000 from a customer. Since court outcome is uncertain and outflow is not yet probable, disclose as a contingent liability.
remember: Contingent liabilities are NEVER recognized on the Balance Sheet face.
If outflow possibility is remote, NO disclosure is needed.
mistakes: Recording a contingent liability on the face of the Balance Sheet instead of disclosing in notes.

quiz.q: How should a contingent liability be presented in financial statements?
o: Recognized on balance sheet liability side
quiz.why: Contingent liabilities are not recognized on the balance sheet; they are disclosed in notes unless the outflow is remote.

quiz.q: In a joint and several liability, how is the portion expected from other parties treated?
quiz.why: The part of a joint obligation expected to be met by other parties is treated as a contingent liability.

topics.title: Contingent Assets
explain: Contingent assets arise from unplanned/unexpected events that create a possibility of economic inflow (e.g. pending legal claims).
An enterprise MUST NOT recognize a contingent asset in financial statements, to avoid recognizing income that may never be realized.
Contingent assets are NOT disclosed in the notes to financial statements.
They are disclosed ONLY in the report of the approving authority (Board of Directors report) where inflow of economic benefits is probable.
When realization of income becomes virtually certain, the asset is no longer contingent and is recognized in financial statements.

flow.title: Treatment of Potential Inflows
steps: If YES recognize asset in financial statements
If probable disclose in Board Report only
Do NOT disclose in financial statement notes

topics.example: Company A files a court case claiming ₹10 lakhs damages. Until court judgment makes recovery virtually certain, no asset is recognized in financial statements.
remember: Contingent assets are NEVER recognized in financial statements.
Disclosed in Board Report ONLY if economic inflow is probable.
mistakes: Disclosing contingent assets in the notes to financial statements like contingent liabilities.

quiz.q: Where should a probable contingent asset be disclosed?
o: In the notes to financial statements
In the Balance Sheet asset side
In the Report of the approving authority (Board Report)
In the Statement of Profit and Loss
quiz.why: Contingent assets are not disclosed in financial statement notes; they appear in the Board Report if inflow is probable.

quiz.q: When can a contingent asset be recognized in financial statements?
o: When realization of income is virtually certain
quiz.why: When realization of income is virtually certain, the asset is no longer contingent and is recognized in financial statements.

topics.title: Measurement & Best Estimate Rules
explain: The provision amount recognized must be the best estimate of expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date.
Estimates are based on management judgment, experience of similar transactions, and independent expert reports.
General provisions should NOT be discounted to present value.
EXCEPTION: Decommissioning, restoration, and similar liabilities recognized as part of Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) cost must be discounted using a pre-tax discount rate.
Provisions are measured before tax; tax consequences are governed by AS 22.

flow.title: Provision Measurement Process
steps: Determine best estimate of settlement expenditure
Consider management judgment and expert reports
If YES apply pre-tax discount rate
If NO do not discount to present value

topics.example: Z Ltd leases a building for 10 years with a restoration clause costing ₹10 lakhs at the end; since it is a restoration liability, provision is recognized at present value.
remember: General provisions are NOT discounted.
Decommissioning/restoration liabilities in PPE ARE discounted at pre-tax rates.
mistakes: Discounting general product warranty provisions to present value.

quiz.q: Under AS 29, which provisions are required to be discounted to present value?
o: Decommissioning and restoration liabilities recognized in PPE
quiz.why: Decommissioning, restoration, and similar liabilities included in PPE cost are discounted to present value.

quiz.q: What type of discount rate should be used for discounting restoration liabilities?
o: Pre-tax discount rate reflecting time value of money
quiz.why: The discount rate must be a pre-tax rate reflecting current market assessments of the time value of money.

topics.title: Future Events, Asset Disposals & Reimbursements
explain: Future events (e.g. tech changes or new laws) affecting settlement cost are included in provision estimation ONLY if supported by objective evidence.
Gains from expected disposal of assets are NOT deducted from the provision amount.
When expenditure is expected to be reimbursed by a third party (e.g. insurance), reimbursement is recognized as a SEPARATE asset.
Reimbursement asset is recognized ONLY when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received upon settling obligation.
The recognized reimbursement asset cannot exceed the provision amount.
In Profit and Loss Statement, the reimbursement expense can be offset against the provision expense.

flow.title: Reimbursement Accounting Process
steps: Is third party reimbursement virtually certain?
If YES recognize separate asset for reimbursement
Ensure asset amount does not exceed provision
Offset reimbursement against expense in P&L

topics.example: Firm A pays ₹1 lakh claim covered by insurance. If insurer confirmation makes payout virtually certain, recognize ₹1 lakh provision liability and ₹1 lakh separate asset.
remember: Reimbursement asset limit = Provision amount.
Asset disposal gains CANNOT be deducted from provision.
mistakes: Netting off the reimbursement asset against the provision liability on the Balance Sheet.

quiz.q: How should expected gains from asset disposals be treated when measuring a provision?
o: Not taken into account in measuring the provision
quiz.why: Gains on expected disposal of assets are not taken into account when measuring a provision.

quiz.q: When can a reimbursement from a third party be recognized as an asset?
o: When it is virtually certain to be received
Whenever an insurance policy is bought
quiz.why: Reimbursement is recognized as a separate asset only when virtually certain to be received upon settling the liability.

topics.title: Changes, Use of Provisions & Restructuring Rules
explain: Provisions must be reviewed at each balance sheet date and adjusted to current best estimates.
If economic outflow is no longer probable, the provision MUST be reversed.
A provision must be used ONLY for expenditures for which it was originally recognized.
Provisions CANNOT be recognized for future operating losses as they do not meet liability criteria.
Restructuring provisions include ONLY direct expenditures necessarily entailed by restructuring and not linked to ongoing activities.
Restructuring provisions EXCLUDE retraining/relocating continuing staff, marketing, and new distribution networks.

flow.title: Restructuring Provision Eligibility
steps: Is cost associated with ongoing activities?
If NO include in restructuring provision

topics.example: Company B restructures and incurs ₹20 lakhs on staff severance and ₹5 lakhs on retraining continuing staff; only severance ₹20 lakhs is included in restructuring provision.
remember: Future operating losses = NO provision.
Restructuring provisions EXCLUDE retraining, marketing, and new systems.
mistakes: Using a warranty provision balance to absorb restructuring expenses.

quiz.q: Can a provision recognized for product warranties be used to pay restructuring legal costs?
o: No, provisions can only be used for specified original purposes
Yes, as both are operational expenses
Yes, if total provision amount is unchanged
quiz.why: A provision shall be used only for expenditures for which it was originally recognized to avoid concealing event impacts.

quiz.q: Which cost is INCLUDED in a restructuring provision?
o: Direct severance costs for redundant staff
quiz.why: Restructuring provisions include only direct expenditures like redundancy/severance pay, excluding retraining, marketing, or new networks.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements & SMC Exemptions
explain: For each class of provision, entities disclose: opening/closing balances, additions, usages, and reversals.
Entities must also disclose nature of obligation, expected timing, uncertainties, and expected reimbursements.
Small and Medium Companies (SMCs) are EXEMPT from opening/closing movement disclosures for provisions.
For contingent liabilities, entities disclose nature, financial effect estimate, uncertainties, and reimbursement possibility unless remote.
In extremely rare cases where disclosure seriously prejudices an entity's position in a dispute, full details can be omitted, provided general nature and reason are stated.

flow.title: Contingent Liability Disclosure Logic
steps: If NO disclose nature and financial effect
Check SMC exemption for provision movement tables

topics.example: If EXOX Ltd pays ₹2.10 crore tax under protest and files an appeal, it discloses ₹2.10 crore as a contingent liability with a brief description.
remember: SMCs are exempt from provision quantitative movement disclosure tables.
Prejudice exemption allows omitting details if general nature and reason are disclosed.
mistakes: Believing Small and Medium Companies (SMCs) are exempt from disclosing contingent liabilities entirely.

quiz.q: What specific disclosure exemption do Small and Medium Companies (SMCs) receive under AS 29?
o: Exempt from specified provision movement disclosure tables
Exempt from accounting for tax under AS 22
Exempt from all disclosures of contingent liabilities
quiz.why: SMCs are exempt from the quantitative opening/closing movement disclosure tables for provisions under AS 29.

quiz.q: When can an entity omit specific dispute details required under AS 29?
o: When disclosure would seriously prejudice the entity's position
When auditors do not request it
quiz.why: In extremely rare cases, if disclosure seriously prejudices the entity's position in a dispute, detailed info can be omitted while disclosing general nature and reason.
